parsed.note_claim: The Prime Minister is not directly elected but is appointed, typically being the leader of the majority party in the House of Representatives.
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: constrained by convention to choose the parliamentarian who is able to command the confidence of the House of Representatives (the lower house). This has almost always been the leader of the majority party or coalition.
parsed.reason: The page confirms the Prime Minister is appointed by the Governor-General based on commanding House confidence, usually the majority party leader.
